plugins.name: ahrena-foundation
plugins.description: The self-hosting core: what an artifact is, where it lives, how it is named, and the skills that create the others. Every other plugin depends on this one.

rules.title: Artifact completeness
rules.statement: An artifact carries no unfilled marker or placeholder, and every section its type requires.

rules.title: Artifact frontmatter
rules.statement: Every artifact opens with frontmatter carrying the fields its type requires and nothing undeclared.

rules.title: Artifact names and paths
rules.statement: Artifact names are kebab-case, carry no type or clade prefix, and sit flat in their type directory.

rules.title: Artifact types and authority
rules.statement: An artifact is exactly one of five types and references only what its type permits.

rules.title: Progressive disclosure
rules.statement: A code block in a skill or agent body is at most 10 lines, and every file in a skill's body is named by a step.

plugins.name: ahrena-engineering-fundamentals
plugins.description: Language-agnostic engineering fundamentals: what justifies an abstraction, which structure must come out regardless, and the complexity signals a script can decide.

rules.title: The aggregate boundary and the event that leaves it
rules.statement: An invariant holds inside one aggregate, a transaction changes one root, aggregates refer to each other by identity, and an event names its root and time.

rules.title: The readable surface
rules.statement: A function body holds at most 30 statements, no statement follows an unconditional exit, and no comment is commented-out code.

rules.title: Platform code holds no client logic
rules.statement: No client logic in platform code: a client's rule is a declaration in its installation, checked by a platform schema; its code enters only by a platform port.

rules.title: A comment points, or it goes
rules.statement: A comment a change adds or edits carries a pointer — an ADR or an issue — or is a permitted exemption; prose with no pointer is a finding the fix removes.

rules.title: The contract is the source
rules.statement: The contract is authored, the code is derived from it or validated against it, and every operation it declares has a test that exercises it.

rules.title: Concerns belong at a boundary
rules.statement: Retry, transaction control, idempotency and metrics are declared once at a boundary; a hand-rolled one inside a body is the defect.

rules.title: Debt that names its issue
rules.statement: A debt marker a change adds or edits names the issue that owns it; a finding with no issue is surfaced and decided, not left in a comment.

rules.title: The domain owns its vocabulary
rules.statement: A domain module imports no mechanism and names no vendor, an aggregate root declares identity and an audit stamp, and no client datum is a literal.

rules.title: Behaviour that belongs to no aggregate
rules.statement: Behaviour whose terms name two aggregates is a stateless domain service under domain/; work that only loads, calls and saves is application, not domain.

rules.title: Duplication at the third copy
rules.statement: The third function body with the same shape and the third table with the same contents are duplicates, counted inside one bounded context.

rules.title: Complexity a script can see
rules.statement: A function nests control flow at most 3 deep and branches on no boolean parameter.

rules.title: Which pattern, and when
rules.statement: A pattern ships only when the situation its catalog entry names is present in the tree and the cheaper alternative in that entry has been ruled out.

rules.title: SOLID as detectable conditions
rules.statement: SOLID conditions that remove structure always apply; the ones that add it apply only when the abstraction trigger in rules/yagni.md is met.

rules.title: The project's language wins
rules.statement: Before naming or creating anything, read the project's ubiquitous language and conventions; the framework default applies only where the project is silent.

rules.title: Parameter objects and value semantics
rules.statement: A callable takes at most 4 parameters, a type declared immutable exposes no mutable field, and a type that defines equality defines hashing.

rules.title: The abstraction trigger
rules.statement: An abstraction ships only with a second real consumer in the tree or a test that requires the seam; an anticipated consumer is not a consumer.

plugins.name: ahrena-engineering-frontend
plugins.description: Frontend built outside-in: a validated wireframe before any code, four layers that stack as stacked pull requests, and a red-to-green test arc per layer, all conforming to the project's component map.

rules.title: The wireframe is the first layer
rules.statement: No component is coded before its wireframe is approved as the first layer; code built against an unvalidated design is defective.

plugins.name: ahrena-engineering-backend
plugins.description: Backend built inside-out: four layers that stack as stacked pull requests — domain, use cases, OLTP, API — with unit TDD red-first at the domain and BDD acceptance tracing to its criteria at the API, all conforming to the project's component map.

plugins.name: ahrena-engineering-data
plugins.description: Data built source→product, contract-first: four layers that stack as stacked pull requests — schema, medallion, expectations, marts — the data contract authored first and the later layers evolving from it, every mart reconciled to its source, all conforming to the project's component map.

rules.title: A mart reconciles to its source
rules.statement: No mart ships without a reconciliation tying its figures to the source its contract pinned; a mart that cannot reconcile to its source is defective, not done.

plugins.name: ahrena-engineering-delivery
plugins.description: Delivery orchestrated issue→stacked-PRs: Athena, the tech-lead, plans a change, routes each concern deterministic-first — a route table, then the Clef decision gate, then a human — delegates to the build clades, runs the develop→Argos loop before each layer opens, and escalates when it is exhausted.

plugins.name: ahrena-engineering-python
plugins.description: What is specific to Python: a distribution per layer under a PEP 420 namespace root, a dependency direction that only runs downward, and an import graph a script proves acyclic.

rules.title: Module boundaries and import acyclicity
rules.statement: Layers import only downward and the first-party import graph is acyclic; moving an import inside a function is the same edge and breaks no cycle.

rules.title: Types that hold, and the defects they do not catch
rules.statement: Python annotates every parameter and return, passes `mypy --strict`, justifies every `Any`, defaults nothing to a mutable, and discards no exception it caught.

plugins.name: ahrena-engineering-typescript
plugins.description: What is specific to TypeScript and the Node and browser code written in it: the type holes a compiler in loose mode lets through, the async mistakes, and the module surface others import.

plugins.name: ahrena-engineering-go
plugins.description: What is specific to Go: errors that are ignored or wrapped wrong, goroutines and contexts that leak, and the interface and nil traps the compiler does not catch.

plugins.name: ahrena-engineering-rust
plugins.description: What is specific to Rust: the panics a library should not take, the unsafe that has to justify itself, the ownership and concurrency choices, and the Result and error surface.

plugins.name: ahrena-engineering-quality
plugins.description: The code-review system: the reviewer and the fixer, the per-discipline review skills, the path router, and the findings and verdict docs they share.

plugins.name: ahrena-engineering-security
plugins.description: Application security as review disciplines: secrets and supply chain, untrusted input, access and sensitive data, and the use of language models and agents.

plugins.name: ahrena-engineering-reliability
plugins.description: Reliability as a review discipline: the timeout a call needs to survive a slow peer, the retry that needs a backoff and a bound, the effect that must stay idempotent under redelivery, the resource that must be released, the dependency that owes a degradation, and the destructive change that must carry a reversal.

plugins.name: ahrena-engineering-observability
plugins.description: Observability as a review discipline: whether a failure leaves a log a human can act on, a critical operation emits a metric or event, a log line carries the what and where to diagnose it, and a service edge carries a correlation id - without ever logging sensitive data.

plugins.name: ahrena-engineering-code-review
plugins.description: The code-review engine: the orchestrator that routes a change to the review lenses it calls for, merges their findings into one verdict, drives the fix-and-re-review loop, and hands an approval to the merge decision.

plugins.name: ahrena-contributing
plugins.description: From the issue to trunk, through two gates and a person landing the change: how a typed issue is opened from its template and a backlog of epics planned, the issue number a branch name carries, the Conventional Commits subject and signature a commit holds, acceptance criteria traced to tests, how a pull request closes its issues, stacks native where the forge has them and run by the framework where it does not, and a trunk only a squash can reach.

rules.title: The branch name carries its issue
rules.statement: A working branch is named for its conventional type, the number of the issue it answers and a kebab-case slug, joined as type/number-slug.

rules.title: What a commit carries
rules.statement: Every commit carries a Conventional Commits subject of at most 72 characters and a signature on the commit object.

rules.title: A decision-record number is free across open pull requests
rules.statement: An open pull request introduces no decision-record number that trunk already carries or that another open pull request also introduces.

rules.title: What a decision record carries
rules.statement: A decision record is numbered without gaps, carries a status from the enum and the four sections, and its supersession names a record that names it back.

rules.title: Two gates, and a review lands the change
rules.statement: An agent starts an issue only when asked, asks for review only after the quality gate passes, and lands a change only after a review approved it.

rules.title: What an issue carries
rules.statement: An issue states what is wrong or missing with the evidence for it, what done looks like, and what it leaves to other issues.

rules.title: A plan closes when its units have, and in order
rules.statement: A pull request does not close an issue with open sub-issues, nor one blocked by an open issue unless it is a layer of a stack.

rules.title: What a pull request carries
rules.statement: A pull request names its branch's issue, closes each issue with its own keyword and nothing it does not name, and has a title trunk can take as a subject.

rules.title: Only a pull request reaches trunk
rules.statement: Trunk is written only by a pull request's squash, and the forge is configured so that nothing else can reach it.

rules.title: A stack is native where it can be, and lands on trunk
rules.statement: A pull request not based on trunk is a layer of a stack, native where the forge has them, the stack lands on trunk, and nothing already landed rides along.

rules.title: Every acceptance criterion is traced to a test
rules.statement: Every issue a pull request closes lists numbered criteria, a test names each one that is not checked by review, and no test names a criterion that is not there.

plugins.name: ahrena-costs
plugins.description: What each issue cost to build: a hook that records a session's tokens and time when it ends, a ledger outside every repository, a price table kept as data, a report per issue in tokens, hours and money, and one cost comment per pull request that local sessions and the CI pipeline both keep up to date.
